name: Ordinary site navigation miscast as application menubar
summary: Ordinary destination links are assigned desktop-command-menu roles without matching menu keyboard and interaction behavior.
recurring_structure: A website navigation list/dropdown adopts menubar/menu/menuitem roles solely because its design resembles a dropdown, without implementing the appropriate keyboard model.
harm_mechanism: Menu roles signal different assistive-technology interaction expectations, while ordinary links may not provide arrow-key or focus movement required for application-menu behavior.
context: Public or product website navigation intended to link to sections, not execute editor-like commands.
applicability: Navigation commands misidentified with application roles when no genuine application menu behavior exists.
legitimate_contexts: Real application command menus with scripted arrow-navigation and correct roles.
A hybrid command palette designed and tested for application-like interaction.

usability: Keyboard expectation mismatch; actual resulting user harm not observed.
accessibility: Potential incorrect semantic role/keyboard behavior, but no WCAG failure or AT output independently demonstrated.
maintainability: Extra scripted application-menu state may be unnecessary for ordinary links; inferred, not measured.

counterexamples.summary: A genuine app editor menubar containing Undo/Cut/Copy commands appropriately uses menu roles with arrow-key interaction.

version_context: WAI official unpinned menu tutorial, Primer docs/live and pinned nav implementation; no runtime test
